title: Weighted Sum of a Tree
summary: Given an integer array parent representing a rooted tree and an integer array nums with node values, calculate the weighted sum of all nodes.
statement: Given an integer array parent representing a rooted tree and an integer array nums with node values, calculate the weighted sum of all nodes. The weight of a node at depth d is its value multiplied by the height of the tree minus the depth plus one. Sum these weights to get the final result.
constraints: parent describes a valid tree rooted at zero; parent indices need not precede child indices.
Root depth is one and tree height is the maximum node depth.
hints: Build children from the parent array because a parent index may appear after its child.
Breadth-first traversal assigns every node depth from root depth one.
The largest assigned depth is the height.
A final pass multiplies each value by the number of levels from that node through the deepest level, inclusive.
editorial: A final pass multiplies each value by the number of levels from that node through the deepest level, inclusive.

tests.explanation: The height is three; applying factors three, two, or one by depth gives total 37.
The four-node chain has factors four through one, giving 4+6+6+4=20.
